children: UBS Group AG (NYSE:UBS) is reshaping its balance sheet and distribution: lifting its debt tender capacity to $4B and setting withdrawal terms, trimming short-term Treasury bullishness while targeting 10y/2y yields, hiring advisor teams adding ~$2.6B AUM, and consolidating China wealth units as it leans on branches for deposits.
: UBS raised its maximum tender offer capacity for debt to $4B from $2B; holders can withdraw tendered notes until 5:00 p.m. ET on Sept. 10, 2026.
: UBS dropped near-term bullish stance on short-dated U.S. Treasuries after being stopped out of 2-year trades. UBS now targets 10-year yield 4.80% and 2-year 4.50%; 2-year ~4.57%.
: UBS hired three advisor teams from Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, adding about $2.6–$2.65 billion in client assets, including a $1.4B Mountain West team and a $750M Bethesda trio.
: UBS will close Shenzhen WE.UBS fund sales unit end-September and absorb its staff into UBS China Securities after missing asset thresholds; firm will consolidate its China wealth platforms.
: UBS says physical branches still key for deposit gathering. Households hold over 60% of system deposits. Branch network expansion by big private banks could support longer-term deposit growth.

title: Weekly Recap: Tender offer $4B and drops bullish view on 2yr Treasuries
